title: Batcher Safety‑Valve Orchestrator: SLO‑aware apply and rollback for automated batching/caching
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build an orchestrator that applies batching and KV prefix‑cache recommendations automatically while enforcing latency and throughput SLO guardrails. The orchestrator must use runtime limiters (circuit/safety valves), SLO‑aware routing to split traffic to candidate configs, and anomaly detection with automatic rollback on regressions. It should integrate with the Optimize advisor, Redwood Console rollout primitives, and Dedicated runtime limit APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor provides candidate batching/cache config and confidence score
Orchestrator can apply config to 1% canary traffic with SLO routing policy
Runtime limiters throttle candidate traffic if p95 latency > SLO or error rate spike > threshold
Anomaly detector flags regressions within 3 minutes and triggers automatic rollback of the candidate
Full audit trail in Console with per-config metrics and a reversible apply action
End‑to‑end test demonstrating cost reduction >=10% on synthetic workload while preserving p95 latency within SLO

tradeoffs: Conservative thresholds reduce cost upside; aggressive thresholds risk customer latency/regressions
Adaptive limiter complexity increases runtime code surface — added shims to isolate in runtime plugin
We prioritize fast rollback over prolonged mitigation paths to keep user experience predictable
design_feedback: PM review (Lin): prefer a phased rollout where Optimize suggests configs but requires PM approval for >=20% traffic
SRE review (Vikram): require circuit breaker that can cut candidate to 0% within 30s of anomaly detection
Console UX (Rae): need a single view showing baseline vs candidate token cost and per-token latency histograms
implementation_notes: Use existing runtime limit APIs: /v1/runtime/limiters - extend to support adaptive windows
SLO checks: p50/p95/p99 latency and 5xx error rate; default window = 3m with 30s evaluation cadence
Anomaly detector: combine z-score + changepoint on token-level latencies and request counts
Routing: implement weighted routing with decay so canary weight grows only when stable for N intervals
Rollback action: immediate 0% weight and enqueue incident with root-cause hints from detector
qa_plan: Unit tests for limiter boundaries and token accounting
Integration tests: staged canary apply -> inject latency regression -> expect rollback within 3m
Load tests on dedicated pool with realistic seq length distribution and cache hit/miss pattern
Chaos tests: simulate runtime plugin failure to ensure fallback to manual apply path
notes: Edge case: models with highly variable decode times can cause false positives; plan to add model-specific baseline profiling
We will expose an "opt-out" label for customers who do not want automated applies
Follow-up: UX for review/approve flow for enterprise customers and audit exports for compliance
